description: Cluster Without IAM Roles for Its Service Accounts
rationale: A pod that cannot assume a role of its own falls back on the instance profile of the node it runs on, so every pod on that node shares one identity: the union of what all the workloads on the node need, granted to each of them, with nothing in CloudTrail to tell which pod made a call. Registering the cluster OIDC issuer as an IAM identity provider, or using EKS pod identity, lets each service account map to its own role, which is what makes least privilege and attribution possible inside the cluster.
remediation: Register the cluster OIDC issuer as an IAM identity provider, or install the EKS pod identity agent, then give each workload a role bound to its own service account and remove the corresponding permissions from the node role
